{{Top|leg|notoc=1}}
{{Quote|You think ''that'' hurts? No, ''this'' hurts.|[[Walon Vau]]|<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>}}
A "'''Keldabe handshake'''" was a euphemistic [[List of phrases and slang/Legends|slang]] term for a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Unarmed combat/Legends|unarmed combat]] technique that consisted of violently gripping a [[Humanoid/Legends|Humanoid]] opponent's groin. Debilitatingly painful for the victim, the technique was noted for its ability to neutralize a [[Human/Legends|Human]] foe with one [[Limb/Legends|hand]]. The term derived its name from [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]], the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]], and a play on the [[handshake]], a common gesture of greeting across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="O66" />

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], during the [[Galactic City spaceport hostage siege|takeover]] of the [[Galactic City Spaceport]] by a group of [[Korun/Legends|Korunnai]] [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorists]], the Mandalorian [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeant]] [[Kal Skirata]] used a "Keldabe handshake" on the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Republic senate's]] [[Senate Head of Public Affairs|Head of Public Affairs]], [[Mar Rugeyan]], when the [[Bureaucrat/Legends|bureaucrat]] disparagingly referred to the [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commando]] [[Fi Skirata|Fi]]—whom Skirata had personally trained on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]—as a grunt, after the [[Commando/Legends|commando]] had rescued several [[Officer/Legends|officers]] of the [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Force]] from a [[Grenade/Legends|grenade]]. Though Skirata did not inflict enough pain to be debilitating, Rugeyan hastily removed himself from the scene when he was released.<ref name="Targets">{{InsiderCite|81|Omega Squad: Targets}}</ref>

Nearly three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later, in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Skirata's Mandalorian contemporary and fellow member of the ''[[Cuy'val Dar]]'', [[Walon Vau]], was hired by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] to cross-train standard [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] with commando skills. During a sparring match with one [[Troop/Legends|trooper]] at [[Arca Company Barracks]], Vau utilized a "Keldabe handshake" that left the veteran clone soldier incapacitated for several moments after.<ref name="O66" />

In [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], early in the [[Yuuzhan Vong War|war]] against the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extra-galactic]] [[Species/Legends|race]] of invaders known as the [[Yuuzhan Vong]], a group of Mandalorians attempted to subdue a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] on the planet [[Birgis]] in order to relay covertly gathered intelligence on the Yuuzhan Vong to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. The pilot, a [[Gender/Legends|female]] Human who struggled heavily due to the belief that the Mandalorians were hostile, was finally brought to heel after the Mandalorian soldier [[Dinua Jeban]] used a "Keldabe handshake" on her.<ref name="APM">''[[Boba Fett: A Practical Man]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The violent grip applied to a being's groin by a Mandalorian was first shown in the ''[[Republic Commando]]'' short story, ''[[Omega Squad: Targets]]'', written by [[Karen Traviss]] and published [[March]] [[2005]] in the [[Star Wars Insider 81|eighty-first issue]] of [[Star Wars Insider]]. A similar situation was again featured in Traviss' [[2006]] [[EBook|e-novella]], ''[[Boba Fett: A Practical Man]]''. However, it was only with the release of Traviss' [[2008]] novel [[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel|''Order 66'']], that the act was identified as the "Keldabe handshake".
